results.source_statement_tex:
\label{lem:1}
Let $(\bV,\bL)$ be the kinetic  Langevin diffusion defined by \eqref{kinetic}.
The modified process $(\bar\bV_t,\bar\bL_t) = (u^{-1/2}\bV_{t/\sqrt{u}},\bL_{t/\sqrt{u}})$
is an kinetic Langevin diffusion as well with associated parameters $\bar\gamma =
\gamma/\sqrt{u}$  and $\bar u=1$.
results.status: Actual inverse-mass kinetic integral equation and Brownian clock scaling proved.
results.note: The changed process has exact unit inverse mass and transformed friction; actual scaled Brownian finite-dimensional laws and coordinate independence are proved.

results.status: Full arbitrary-shift actual Brownian law contraction proved; printed first prefactor corrected.
results.note: Equation exp2 is proved for the actual canonical Brownian solution and true Wasserstein infimum. The source claim alpha≤sqrt(2)/gamma is false as printed; the unshifted bound has prefactor sqrt(2). The common initial velocity law and finite second moments are explicit.

results.source_statement_tex:
\label{th:3}
Assume that the function $f$ is twice differentiable with a Hessian matrix
$\nabla^2f$ satisfying $m\bfI_p\preceq \nabla^2f(\bx)\preceq M\bfI_p$ for every
$\bx\in\RR^p$.
In addition, let the initial condition of the KLMC algorithm be drawn from the product
distribution $\mu = \mathcal N(\mathbf 0_p,\bfI_p)\otimes \nu_0$.  For every $\gamma\ge
\sqrt{m+M}$ and $h\le m/(4\gamma M)$, the distribution $\nu_k$ of the $k$th iterate
$\bvartheta_k$ of the KLMC algorithm \eqref{KLMC} satisfies
\begin{align}
W_2(\nu_k,\pi)
&\le \sqrt{2}\Big(1-\frac{0.75mh}{\gamma}\Big)^kW_2(\nu_0,\pi) +
\frac{Mh\sqrt{2p}}{m}.
\end{align}
results.status: Unconditional actual correlated-Gaussian KLMC Wasserstein theorem proved.
results.note: The implemented chain uses the true correlated innovation stream and independent thermal initialization. Stationary reference paths, source laws, local error, recurrence and the true initial Wasserstein infimum are all derived.

results.source_statement_tex:
\label{th:4}
Assume that, for some constants $m,M,M_2>0$, the function $f$ is
$m$-strongly convex, its gradient is $M$-Lipschitz, and its Hessian is $M_2$-Lipschitz for the spectral norm.
In addition, let the initial condition of the second-order KLMC algorithm be drawn
from the product distribution $\mu = \mathcal N(\mathbf 0_p,\bfI_p)\otimes \nu_0$.
For every 
$$
\gamma\ge \sqrt{m+M}\quad \text{and}\quad h\le \frac{m}{5\gamma M}\wedge
\frac{m}{4\sqrt{5p}\,M_2}, 
$$
the distribution
$\nu_k^{\rm KLMC2}$  of the $k$th iterate $\bvartheta_k^{\rm KLMC2}$ of the
second-order KLMC algorithm \eqref{KLMC2} satisfies\footnote{One can see
from the proof that $e^{-p/2}$ in this inequality can be replaced
by the smaller quantity $e^{-\frac{m^2}{160 M_2^2h^2}}$.
}
\begin{align}
		W_2(\nu_k^{\rm KLMC2},\pi)
		&\le \sqrt{2}\Big(1-\frac{mh}{4\gamma}\Big)^{k}W_2(\nu_0,\pi)		
		+\frac{2h^2{M_2p}}{m}+\frac{h^2 M\sqrt{2Mp}}{{m}}
		+ \frac{8M}{m}\, h e^{-p/2} .\label{s5:1}
\end{align}
results.status: Unconditional actual four-kernel KLMC2 Wasserstein theorem proved, with exact all-dimension moment and corrected printed simplification.
results.note: All actual reference paths, normalized Gibbs stationarity, true past/future independence, four-kernel Gaussian law, pointwise/L² numerical correspondence, repaired stochastic Hessian comparison, local Taylor error, geometric iteration, output-law independence and the true initial Wasserstein infimum are proved internally. The exact bound retains sqrt(p²+2p), including p=1. The printed 2M2*p simplification is proved only with p≥2 stated explicitly. The exact tail 8(M-m)h/m*exp(-(alpha-p)/8), alpha=(m/(4M2h))², implies both the printed 8Mh/m*exp(-p/2) and the stronger footnote inverse-step-square tail 8(M-m)h/m*exp(-m²/(160M2²h²)).

results.note: The shared forcing cancels in the actual integral equations. The exact prefactor and max-branch exponent follow from centered strong-smooth interpolation; the law proof integrates this pathwise bound on true couplings.

results.note: The positive square-root denominator is explicit. Exact quadratic solutions show the slow exponent is sharp; the repeated-root boundary has an unavoidable polynomial prefactor and is not evaluated through the singular displayed constant.

results.source_statement_tex:
\label{prop:2}
  Assume that, for some constants $m,M,M_2>0$, the function $f$ is
$m$-strongly convex, its gradient is $M$-Lipschitz, and its Hessian is $M_2$-Lipschitz for the spectral norm. If the parameter $\gamma$ and the step size $t$ of the kinetic Langevin diffusion are such that
  $$t\le\frac{1}{5\gamma},$$
  then
$$
 \left\|\bfP^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}
     \bV_t-\hat{\bV}_t \\
      \bL_t-\hat{\bL}_t
\end{bmatrix}\right\|_{{\LL}_2}\le0.25\times t^3(M_2\sqrt{p^2+2p}+M^{3/2}\sqrt{p}).
$$
results.status: Actual stationary kinetic local error and exact implemented KLMC2 identification proved.
results.note: Stationarity of the exact reference, implicit in the source moment argument, is explicit and proved for the canonical reference segments. The exact cubic transformed error retains sqrt(p²+2p) and applies to the implemented four-kernel numerical step.

results.source_statement_tex:
For any time step $t>0$ we have
$$\|\hat{\bV}_t-\bV_t\|_{{\LL}_2}\le\frac{t^3(M_2\sqrt{p^2+2p}+M^{3/2}\sqrt{p})}{6},$$
$$\|\hat{\bL}_t-\bL_t\|_{{\LL}_2}\le\frac{t^4(M_2\sqrt{p^2+2p}+M^{3/2}\sqrt{p})}{24}.
$$
results.status: Exact cubic velocity and quartic position errors proved for the actual stationary reference.
results.note: The two component constants 1/6 and 1/24 follow from genuine Taylor remainders, L4 time-integral estimates, actual Gaussian fourth moments, Gibbs score moments and exact mild/kinematic equations.

results.source_statement_tex:
\label{prop:3}
 Assume that, for some constants $m,M,M_2>0$, the function $f$ is
$m$-strongly convex, its gradient is $M$-Lipschitz, and its Hessian is $M_2$-Lipschitz for the spectral norm. If the parameter $\gamma$ and the step size $t$ of the kinetic Langevin diffusion satisfy the inequalities
$$
\gamma^2\ge m+M,\qquad t\le\frac{1}{5\gamma\varkappa},
$$
then, for  the $(2p)\times (2p)$ matrix $\bfP$ defined in \eqref{pp-1}, and for every
$a\ge 5p$, it holds
  \begin{align}
       \left\|\bfP^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}
     \hat{\bV}_t - \Tilde\bV_t \\
      \hat{\bL}_t - \Tilde\bL_t
\end{bmatrix}\right\|_{{\LL}_2}
&\le
\left(1-\frac{mt}{2\gamma}+\frac{M_2\sqrt{a}\,t^2}{\gamma}\right)
\left\|\bfP^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}
     \bV_0-\Tilde{\bV}_0  \\
      \bL_0-\Tilde{\bL}_0
\end{bmatrix}\right\|_{{\LL}_2}\\
&\qquad + \sqrt{2}\,t^2(M-m)e^{-(a-p)/8}.
  \end{align}
results.status: Repaired actual four-kernel KLMC2 comparison proved with every stochastic Hessian difference retained.
results.note: The displayed subtraction in the source omits fresh Hessian-noise terms. The checked repair groups both deterministic and stochastic corrections into a genuine free-OU velocity, proves its actual Gaussian marginal from past/future independence, and applies the cutoff without Hessian/noise independence.

results.status: Actual canonical four-kernel KLMC2 recurrence, its geometric iteration, and projected source bias proved.
results.note: The recurrence is derived for the actual canonical numerical and stationary reference chains; there is no assumed local-error or abstract recurrence premise in the canonical result. The scalar iteration chooses alpha=(m/(4M2h))², absorbs M2*sqrt(alpha)*h≤m/4, sums the genuine local cubic and Gaussian-tail terms, and retains the exact sqrt(p²+2p) moment. The per-coupling position bound is projected before the final theorem takes the true transport infimum. Both the sharper inverse-step-square tail and its exp(-p/2) relaxation are checked.
